passages.text: Then Job replied to the LORD: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke to the LORD.
Job answered the LORD.
Job said, “You are all-powerful.
You can do everything.
No one can stop Your plans.
No one can defeat Your purpose.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֖עַן אִיּ֥וֹב אֶת־ יְהוָ֗ה וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ יָדַעְתָּ כִּי־ כֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וְלֹא־ יִבָּצֵ֖ר מִמְּךָ֣ מְזִמָּֽה׃

passages.text: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
passages.sermon:
God asked a question.
God said, “Who is this who hides My counsel without knowledge?”
Job answered God.
Job said, “I spoke about things I did not understand.”
These things were too wonderful for me.
I did not know them.
passages.original: מִ֤י זֶ֨ה׀ מַעְלִ֥ים עֵצָ֗ה בְּֽלִ֫י דָ֥עַת לָכֵ֣ן הִ֭גַּדְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין נִפְלָא֥וֹת מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְלֹ֣א אֵדָֽע׃

passages.text: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Job.
God said, “Listen now.
I will speak.
I will ask you questions.
You will answer Me.”
passages.original: שְֽׁמַֽע־ נָ֭א וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job says he heard about God before.
Job says he heard about God with his ears.
Now Job has seen God.
Job says his own eyes have seen God.
passages.original: לְשֵֽׁמַע־ אֹ֥זֶן שְׁמַעְתִּ֑יךָ וְ֝עַתָּ֗ה עֵינִ֥י רָאָֽתְךָ׃

passages.text: Therefore I retract my words, and I repent in dust and ashes.”
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is humble.
Job says, "I take back my words."
Job says, "I repent."
Job sits in dust and ashes.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֭ן אֶמְאַ֣ס וְנִחַ֑מְתִּי עַל־ עָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר׃פ

passages.text: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Job.
The LORD then spoke to Eliphaz the Temanite.
The LORD said, “I am angry with you, Eliphaz.
I am also angry with your two friends.
You and your friends did not speak accurately about Me.
My servant Job spoke about Me correctly.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל־ אִיּ֑וֹב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ אֱלִיפַ֣ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֗י חָרָ֨ה אַפִּ֤י בְךָ֙ וּבִשְׁנֵ֣י רֵעֶ֔יךָ כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Eliphaz the Temanite and his two friends.
The LORD was angry with them.
The LORD said they had not spoken accurately about Him.
Job, the LORD’s servant, had spoken accurately about the LORD.
The LORD gave them a command.
He told them to take seven bulls and seven rams.
He told them to go to His servant Job.
He told them to offer a burnt offering for themselves.
He said Job would pray for them.
The LORD said He would accept Job’s prayer.
The LORD said He would not punish them for their folly.
He repeated that they had not spoken accurately about Him.
He said Job, His servant, had spoken accurately about Him.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֡ה קְחֽוּ־ לָכֶ֣ם שִׁבְעָֽה־ פָרִים֩ וְשִׁבְעָ֨ה אֵילִ֜ים וּלְכ֣וּ׀ אֶל־ עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֤ם עוֹלָה֙ בַּֽעַדְכֶ֔ם וְאִיּ֣וֹב עַבְדִּ֔י יִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֧י אִם־ פָּנָ֣יו אֶשָּׂ֗א לְבִלְתִּ֞י עֲשׂ֤וֹת עִמָּכֶם֙ נְבָלָ֔ה כִּ֠י לֹ֣א דִבַּרְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֛י נְכוֹנָ֖ה כְּעַבְדִּ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s request.
passages.sermon:
Eliphaz was from Teman.
Bildad was from Shuah.
Zophar was from Naamah.
These three men were friends of Job.
The LORD had spoken to them.
The LORD gave them instructions.
Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar went to Job.
They did what the LORD told them to do.
The LORD accepted Job’s prayer for his friends.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ אֱלִיפַ֨ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֜י וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י צֹפַר֙ הַנַּ֣עֲמָתִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ פְּנֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Job was a servant of the LORD.
Job prayed for his friends.
After Job prayed, the LORD restored Job’s prosperity.
The LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת־ שְׁבִית אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַ֧יֹּסֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה׃

passages.text: All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
passages.sermon:
Job suffered much adversity from the LORD.
All his brothers came to him.
All his sisters came to him.
All his former acquaintances came to him.
They entered his house.
They ate bread with him in his house.
They showed him sympathy.
They comforted him for all the trouble the LORD had brought upon him.
Each person gave Job a piece of silver.
Each person gave Job a gold ring.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל־ אֶחָ֨יו וְכָל־ אַחְיֹתָיו וְכָל־ יֹדְעָ֣יו לְפָנִ֗ים וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ עִמּ֣וֹ לֶחֶם֮ בְּבֵיתוֹ֒ וַיָּנֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ וַיְנַחֲמ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עַ֚ל כָּל־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיִּתְּנוּ־ ל֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ קְשִׂיטָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאִ֕ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם זָהָ֖ב אֶחָֽד׃ס

passages.text: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
passages.sermon:
The LORD blessed Job.
The LORD gave Job greater blessings in his later life than in his earlier life.
Job owned 14,000 sheep.
Job owned 6,000 camels.
Job owned 1,000 yoke of oxen.
Job owned 1,000 female donkeys.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֗ה בֵּרַ֛ךְ אֶת־ אַחֲרִ֥ית אִיּ֖וֹב מֵרֵאשִׁת֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי־ ל֡וֹ אַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר אֶ֜לֶף צֹ֗אן וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ גְּמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶֽלֶף־ צֶ֥מֶד בָּקָ֖ר וְאֶ֥לֶף אֲתוֹנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.
passages.sermon:
Job was a man who suffered greatly, but God restored him.
God blessed Job after his suffering.
Job had seven sons.
Job had three daughters.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי־ ל֛וֹ שִׁבְעָ֥נָה בָנִ֖ים וְשָׁל֥וֹשׁ בָּנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.
passages.sermon:
Job had three daughters.
He named his first daughter Jemimah.
He named his second daughter Keziah.
He named his third daughter Keren-happuch.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־ הָֽאַחַת֙ יְמִימָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית קְצִיעָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית קֶ֥רֶן הַפּֽוּךְ׃

passages.text: No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.
passages.sermon:
Job had daughters.
Job’s daughters were very beautiful.
No other women in the land were as beautiful as Job’s daughters.
Job was their father.
Job gave his daughters an inheritance.
Job gave this inheritance to his daughters among their brothers.
passages.original: וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א נָשִׁ֥ים יָפ֛וֹת כִּבְנ֥וֹת אִיּ֖וֹב בְּכָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם אֲבִיהֶ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
passages.sermon:
Job was a man.
God restored Job after his suffering.
After this, Job lived 140 years.
Job saw his children.
Job saw his grandchildren.
Job saw his great-grandchildren.
Job saw his great-great-grandchildren.
Job saw four generations of his family.
passages.original: וַיְחִ֤י אִיּוֹב֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־ זֹ֔את מֵאָ֥ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיַּרְא אֶת־ בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י בָנָ֔יו אַרְבָּעָ֖ה דֹּרֽוֹת׃

passages.text: And so Job died, old and full of years.
passages.sermon:
Job was a man.
Job lived a long life.
Job became old.
Job was satisfied with his years.
Job died.
